learning_outcomes.text: Identify and classify bilinear forms and real quadratic forms.
Solve, using symbolic and numerical calculation, problems of maximums, minimums, and constrained extremes.
Decompose matrices, geometrically interpret the result, and apply it to problem-solving.
Use basic concepts, results, and techniques in affine and Euclidean geometry.
Relate the intuitive concept of rigid body motion (in the plane or real space) to orthogonal transformations.
Explain the concept and know the usual techniques of least squares fitting.
Solve Advanced Mathematics problems using computational tools.

syllabus_topics: Orthogonality. Relation to rigid body motion
Calculation of extremes of functions of several variables
Numerical methods for the calculation of extremes
teaching_methods: Virtual expository sessions (videos, presentations, instructional texts, self-assessment questionnaires)
Presential expository classes (doubt resolution, theoretical results, examples)
Virtual classroom practices (video viewing, questionnaires, forum participation)
Presential classroom practices (exercises and tasks, individual or group)
Virtual laboratory practices (solving exercises with MatLab)
Presential laboratory practices (solving exercises with MatLab)
Tutorials (forums, personal or group virtual tutorials via Teams)
assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) is calculated as: NF = 0.2 NL + 0.2 NA + 0.5 NC + 0.1 NCv. NL is the laboratory practices grade, NA is the classroom practices grade, NC is the average of partial exams (0.4 P1 + 0.6 P2) or the global test grade (PG), and NCv is the virtual campus tasks grade. To pass, NF must be >= 5, NC >= 3.5, and NL >= 3.5. If these minimums are not met, the final grade will be min(NF, NC, NL). For differentiated evaluation, NF = 0.2 NL + 0.6 NC + 0.2 NOL.
